terms.meaning: A reusable block of screen code that is shown and updated by the app.
The inputs a component receives from its parent, such as the component data and action functions.
A basic shape, here either a box or a cylinder.
One shape definition with its size, position, rotation, material and repeat settings.
The record of where a value came from: evidence, manual entry, or default.
A saved set of recipes that can be reused on other components.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the editor
sections.what: Brings in the state hook, the assembly helper functions, the recipe types, the data types and the material list used by the editor.
sections.why: Likely reason: the editor needs the same rules and material names as the rest of the app.

sections.name: AssemblyEditorProps
sections.title: What the editor receives from its parent
sections.what: Lists the component, templates, busy flag, and the save, template, delete and assign actions the parent must provide.
sections.why: Likely reason: the parent owns saving, so this editor only edits and reports.
sections.watch_out: The editor does not save anything by itself, so a missing or broken action means nothing is stored.

sections.name: VECTOR_LABELS
sections.title: Field labels with units
sections.what: Gives each kind of measurement a readable label with its unit, such as metres or degrees.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows the unit next to every number so users enter the right thing.
sections.watch_out: Rotation is entered in degrees but stored in radians, so the label must stay consistent with that conversion.

sections.name: PROVENANCE_HELP
sections.title: Tooltip text for number origins
sections.what: Stores the explanation shown when a user hovers over the evidence, manual or default label of a value.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows how far a number can be trusted.
sections.watch_out: A new origin label needs matching text here or the tooltip will be empty.

sections.name: AssemblyEditor (part 1)
sections.title: Draft state, reset and validation
sections.what: Keeps working copies of the recipes and compares them with the saved version to show unsaved changes. Provides a reset button and runs validation before any save or template action, showing an error message if the input is wrong.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets users try changes safely before committing them.
sections.watch_out: The unsaved check compares text, so reordering recipes can make the editor report changes that do not matter.

sections.name: AssemblyEditor (part 2)
sections.title: Recipe fields, material and repeat controls
sections.what: Shows each recipe's role, shape type, dimensions, position, rotation, material, repeat count and offset. A material can be set to a custom key. A remove button asks for confirmation before deleting a recipe from the draft.
sections.why: Likely reason: removal is confirmed because the change is only a draft until saved.
sections.watch_out: Custom material keys are kept but display with a generic profile, so they may look different from the standard materials.

sections.name: AssemblyEditor (part 3)
sections.title: Save, reset and template library
sections.what: Provides buttons to add a box or cylinder, save the assembly, create or update a named template, choose and edit a saved template, assign it to the selected component, and delete it. Assign and delete both ask for confirmation.
sections.why: Likely reason: templates can be reused on many components, and the on-screen note says updating a template does not change assets already using it.
sections.watch_out: Add buttons are disabled at the recipe and expanded-part limits, so a user at the limit cannot add anything without first removing a recipe.

summary: The form inside the 3D view where a user edits a component's assembly recipes, saves them, and manages reusable templates.
purpose: Lets an expert change the shapes that make up a component and see where each number came from.
why: Likely reason: edits stay in a draft until saved, so a mistake does not change the model by accident.
how: Starts from the component's saved recipes as editable drafts. Each change updates the draft and marks it as changed. Validation runs before saving. Save, template and assign buttons call functions supplied by the parent, and confirmation pop-ups guard destructive actions like removing or deleting.
inputs: A component, the list of templates, a busy flag, and five action functions supplied by the parent.
outputs: Calls to the save, template, assign and delete actions, plus a validation message when input is wrong. The editor does not save data itself.
risks: Reset and template edits discard unsaved changes. The limits of 256 recipes and 4,096 expanded parts are enforced only by disabling buttons. Custom material keys render with a generic material. One long intro paragraph at line 58 is cut off in the packet, so its exact wording is unknown.
debug: If saving fails, read the red validation message and check the matching action in the parent. If numbers look wrong, compare the provenance label and the component's saved parts. If buttons stay disabled, check the busy flag and the count limits.
